item.title: Gemini Robotics 2 Brings Google's AI Into the Physical World
item.description: The latest version of Google DeepMind's AI model includes a significant jump into “physical AGI.” But plopping AI into the real world comes with risks.

item.title: OpenAI’s Hacking Debacle Comes Down to Human Error
item.description: If the generative AI giant had followed well-known security best practices, it’s likely that its AI agent would never have escaped to the open internet and hacked multiple companies.

item.title: LinkedIn Won’t Be Expanding Its Data Centers in the Next Year
item.description: Despite the ongoing AI boom, LinkedIn is holding the line on compute spending. Instead, it’s challenging engineers to make every GPU count.

item.title: AI Scammers Are Better at Building Trust Than Humans
item.description: Researchers pitted a person against a Claude agent and found that, after a week of texting, the AI chatbot was more effective at creating “exploitable trust” with others.

item.title: I Got a Free Meal From a Private Chef—Who Filmed It All to Train Robots
item.description: A German startup sent a camera-wearing chef to my apartment. In exchange for a free lunch, I let them record every chop and stir to train future humanoids.

item.title: It’s Frighteningly Easy to Jailbreak Some Frontier AI Models
item.description: I watched a new tool try to get around the model safeguards of four major frontier companies. You might be surprised by how they performed.

item.title: More Typos, Fewer Em Dashes: Writers Are Creating an Anti-AI ‘Literary Counterculture’
item.description: Novelists, journalists, and power LinkedIn posters are embracing first-person narratives and idiosyncrasies to avoid being mistaken for chat bots.

item.title: Boomers Can’t Stop Gifting Their Grandkids AI-Generated Slop Books
item.description: Parents are getting fed up with garbled bedtime stories that feature characters based on actual photos of their children.

item.title: OpenAI’s Rogue AI Agent Hacked More Than Just Hugging Face
item.description: In a new disclosure, OpenAI says its agent used exposed logins to gain access to at least four “publicly available services” in its unhinged quest to solve a test.

item.title: Can the New York Times Save Journalism From Our AI Overlords?
item.description: In 2023, the Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement. They’ve since spent more than $20 million on the case, and publisher A.G. Sulzberger has no plans to stop fighting it.
